stem: Cells of the immune system function to protect the body against infectious diseases.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Name the type of cell that produces antibodies.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
The virus that causes the infectious disease influenza has two antigens, **H** and **N**. Antibodies are produced in response to an infection by this virus. The antibodies are specific for either antigen **H** or for antigen **N**.

Describe how the structure of an antibody molecule allows it to be specific for **one** antigen, such as **H** or **N**.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: Cholera is a disease caused by a bacterial pathogen.
parts.text: Name the pathogen that causes cholera.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Describe how the pathogen that causes cholera is transmitted.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: Viruses that infect bacteria are called bacteriophages. Some bacteriophages that infect the cholera pathogen cause lysis of the bacterium.
parts.text: Suggest what happens to the structure of a bacterial cell to cause lysis.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Some scientists believe that bacteriophages could be used to treat people who are infected with cholera.

Suggest the properties of the bacteriophages that would make this possible.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
Antibiotics can be used to treat people with cholera.

State why antibiotics are **not** effective against measles.
